_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 16 (Hagar). Saadia-specific moves: v.7 שור=חגר 'the road to Hajar/Hegra' (Arabian peninsula identification); v.11 צ'עפך='your weakness/affliction' for עניך; v.13 'the Power who sees' (אלטאיק אלנאצ'ר) — anti-anthropomorphic substitute for אל ראי; v.14 קדש=רקים 'Rekem' (Petra) consistent with B14:7.

translations.1: And Sarai the wife of Abram had not borne him [children]; and she had an Egyptian maidservant whose name was Hagar.
translations.2: And Sarai said to Abram: 'Behold, God has held me back from bearing — enter to my maidservant; perhaps my house will be built up from her.' And Abram accepted the words of Sarai.
translations.3: And Sarai the wife of Abram took Hagar the Egyptian, her maidservant, after ten years of Abram's dwelling in the land of Canaan; and she gave her to Abram her husband, to be a wife for him.
translations.4: And he came to Hagar, and she conceived; and when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was diminished in her eyes.
translations.5: And Sarai said to Abram: 'My wrong is upon you! I gave you my maidservant; and when she saw that she had conceived, I was diminished in her eyes. May God judge between me and you.'
translations.6: Abram said to her: 'Behold, your maidservant is in your hand; do to her what is good in your eyes.' And Sarai afflicted her, until she fled from before her.
translations.7: And the angel of God found her by a spring of water in the wilderness — by the spring on the road to Hajar (Shur).
translations.8: And he said: 'O Hagar, maidservant of Sarai, whence have you come, and whither do you go?' She said: 'From before Sarai my mistress I am fleeing.'
translations.9: And the angel of God said to her: 'Return to your mistress, and serve under her hands.'
translations.10: Then he said to her: 'I shall greatly multiply your offspring, so that it shall not be counted from its abundance.'
translations.11: And he said to her: 'Behold, you are with child; you shall bear a son, and you shall name him Ishmael — for God has heard your affliction.
translations.12: And he shall be a wild one among people; his hand against all, and the hand of all against him; and in the presence of all his brothers shall he dwell.'
translations.13: And she named the name of God, who had appeared to her: 'You are the Power who sees' — for she said: 'I have seen here Your mercy, after my vision of misery.'
translations.14: Therefore the well was called the Well of the Living One who Sees; behold, it is between Rekem (Kadesh) and Bered.
translations.15: And Hagar bore to Abram a son; and Abram named his son, whom Hagar had borne him, Ishmael.
translations.16: And Abram was a son of eighty-six years when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.
